sources.excerpt: Elected June 2, 2026, to fill the vacancy due to the death of Doug LaMalfa, January 6, 2026.

sources.title: Biography | Congressman James Gallagher
sources.excerpt: James was elected in June to the 119th Congress, by special election, to fill the vacancy caused by the death of CA District 1 Representative Doug LaMalfa.

sources.title: Biography | Congressman James Gallagher
sources.excerpt: Prior to being elected to Congress, James served in the California State Assembly from December 2014 - May 2026, where he served as Assembly Minority Leader for 4 years.

sources.title: Biography | Congressman James Gallagher
sources.excerpt: Before being election to the State Assembly, he proudly served his community for 6 years as a member of the Sutter County Board of Supervisors.

sources.title: Biography | Congressman James Gallagher
sources.excerpt: James earned his Bachelor of Arts Degree at UC Berkeley, where he was Editor-in-Chief of The Patriot, a nationally recognized conservative news magazine, and was elected to the student senate. Upon graduation, he served in the prestigious Assembly Fellowship Program in Sacramento.

sources.title: Biography | Congressman James Gallagher
sources.excerpt: Upon completion of the fellowship, he obtained his law degree from UC Davis, graduating at the top of his class. Gallagher is a partner in his family’s farming business as well as a practicing attorney, focusing on agricultural law.

sources.excerpt: Vacancy resulting from the death of Doug LaMalfa.

sources.title: Special Election Proclamation by the Governor of the State of California（1st Congressional District）
sources.excerpt: I, GAVIN NEWSOM, Governor of the State of California, do hereby proclaim and order that a special election shall be held on the 4th day of August 2026, within the 1st Congressional District of the State, to fill the vacancy in the office of the U.S. House of Representatives from said district resulting from the death of Representative Doug LaMalfa.

sources.title: Assembly Journal, June 10, 2026（California State Assembly）
sources.excerpt: I am forwarding a letter of resignation from Assembly Member James Gallagher, Assembly District 3, effective June 9, 2026, upon close of business.

sources.title: James Gallagher '07 Elected to Congress | School of Law（UC Davis）
sources.excerpt: James Gallagher ’07 has been elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, filling the Northern California District 1 seat long held by Rep. Doug LaMalfa, who died in January 2026.

sources.title: James Gallagher '07 Elected to Congress | School of Law（UC Davis）
sources.excerpt: A state Assembly member for 12 years, Gallagher served as Assembly Republican Minority Leader from 2022-25. Before the Assembly, Gallagher served on the Sutter County Board of Supervisors.

sources.title: James Gallagher sworn in to finish LaMalfa’s term in the House – Roll Call
sources.excerpt: Born in Yuba City, Gallagher earned a bachelor’s degree from the University of California, Berkeley. He got his law degree from UC Davis before he signed on to a practice centered on business and agriculture.

sources.title: James Gallagher sworn in to finish LaMalfa’s term in the House – Roll Call
sources.excerpt: First elected to the California State Assembly in 2014, Gallagher represented an inland district centered on the city of Chico. He was appointed GOP leader in 2022. He also spent six years on the Board of Supervisors for Sutter County, where he lives.

sources.title: James Gallagher sworn in to finish LaMalfa’s term in the House – Roll Call
sources.excerpt: He stepped down as caucus leader in September, according to ABC News affiliate KRCR.

sources.title: Speaker’s Majority Grows as California Republican Joins Ranks（Bloomberg Government）
sources.excerpt: “It will be the first time ever that I’ve been in the majority,” Gallagher, 45, said in a farewell speech Monday to the Democratic-led California Assembly.

sources.title: James Gallagher sworn in to finish LaMalfa’s term in the House – Roll Call
sources.excerpt: Gallagher is also a partner in his family’s rice farm.
